title: Telnet exposed
reason: Telnet sends credentials and data in cleartext, so anyone on the network path can read them.

title: FTP exposed
reason: FTP sends credentials in cleartext and often allows anonymous access.
fix: Use SFTP/FTPS, disable anonymous login, restrict by firewall.

title: SMB/NetBIOS exposed
reason: SMB is a common target for credential attacks, relay and wormable bugs.
fix: Block SMB at the perimeter and restrict to trusted hosts.

title: RDP exposed
reason: Exposed RDP is a frequent target for brute force and remote exploits.
fix: Put RDP behind a VPN, enforce MFA and Network Level Authentication.

title: VNC exposed
reason: VNC often has weak or no authentication and weak encryption.
fix: Tunnel through SSH or VPN and require strong passwords.

title: Database exposed
reason: Databases should not be reachable from untrusted networks.
fix: Bind to localhost or an internal network and firewall the port.

title: Legacy r-service exposed
reason: rexec, rlogin and rsh use cleartext and weak host-based trust.
fix: Disable the service and use SSH.

title: Possible backdoor shell
reason: A service identified as a bind shell gives remote command access with no authentication.
fix: Isolate the host and investigate. Treat it as compromised.

title: NFS/RPC exposed
reason: Exposed NFS or RPC can leak shares and system information.
fix: Restrict to trusted hosts and review the export list.

title: X11 exposed
reason: An open X11 server can allow remote screen capture and keystroke access.
fix: Disable TCP listening and use SSH X11 forwarding.

title: Java RMI exposed
reason: Misconfigured RMI registries can allow remote code execution.
fix: Restrict access and review the RMI configuration.

title: TFTP/SNMP exposed
reason: TFTP has no authentication, and SNMP often uses default community strings.
fix: Restrict access and change default community strings.

title: Plain HTTP (no TLS)
reason: Traffic is unencrypted, so logins and session cookies can be intercepted.
fix: Serve over HTTPS and redirect HTTP to it.
